angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 730,485 km at 51.67 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 19.3527 +/- 0.0223 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 51.67 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.05 solar radii from Vican & Schneider (2014), ApJ 780, 154, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729): 730,485 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.059 (1.019 to 1.099) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6032 K from McDonald et al. (2012), MNRAS 427, 343, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). Spin inclination 59 degrees and rotation period 1.3571 d from Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2, the values of the ZDI inversion (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald et al. (2012), MNRAS 427, 343, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/v1358-orionis.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.421, rounded to two decimals
